name: Valet parking for events

pf.license.need: The company's own registration and its insurance: garage-keepers liability for the cars, and general liability. Where the city or the venue requires a valet permit or a parking permit for the event, the company files it. Each attendant holds a valid driver's license for the class the lot's cars need, where the rules ask.
pf.license.per event: Where the city or the venue requires a permit for the valet stand or the street, the contract says who files it and by when.
pf.license.who holds it: The company holds its registration, its insurance and any valet permit. Each attendant holds their own driver's license, where the rules ask.
pf.license.manager on site: A lot lead is on site for each event, and the venue's own parking rules are followed.
what to ask: The company's registration number, if the state issues one
The garage-keepers insurance certificate, its amount and end date
The venue's or city's valet permit, if one is required, and its due date
pf.license.how it's checked: Nothing is looked up. Rosie keeps the numbers and dates the owner gives, and the owner keeps the papers. Rosie never checks a license, permit or insurance.
pf.license.blocks going live: None from Rosie: no booking is held or refused because a permit can't be read. The owner decides what the company offers.
pf.license.renewals: None kept by Rosie: the owner keeps the end dates and the renewals.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Garage-keepers and general liability insurance; the certificate goes to any venue that asks. Rosie never verifies it.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the venue's rules or the state's form ask. Rosie never verifies them.

pf.services.capacity: One lot per night. Two attendants park up to 100 cars; three park up to 200. Attendants never drive a car on a public road beyond the lot.
pf.services.nobody needs to be there: Never: a car is handed back to the person who holds the ticket, checked against it.
pf.services.online: Planning calls by video or phone.

stops the booking.words: A crash, a car on fire, or someone hurt at the lot right now
stops the booking.says: If anyone is hurt or in danger, call 911 now and move everyone away from the cars. Do not move a car with someone in it.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

stops the booking.words: A gas smell or a fuel spill in the lot now
stops the booking.says: Move everyone away from the spill and call 911.

safety steps, then the booking goes on.words: A car that won't start or a flat in the lot
safety steps, then the booking goes on.says: The attendant tells the lot lead. The car is moved only by the lead, and the owner is called.

pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, a crash, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first. Attendants never drive a car with a child or a pet unattended, and never drive a car beyond the lot.

before the main visit.step: The valet contract, signed on the secure page
before the main visit.timing: At booking, before any money is taken. It has the date, hours, car count, the deposit, the cancel schedule, the rest, the lot's rules, and who files any valet permit. Not signed in 24 hours: the booking is let go.
Sam sends it by 7 days before. Not sent: the venue may refuse the valet stand; that's the business's side.

before the main visit.step: The valet permit, or the street or lot closure
before the main visit.for: Where the city or the venue requires one
before the main visit.timing: Filed by the organizer or the company, as the contract says, by the rules' due date. Not filed: no valet stand on the street.
7 days before, on the secure page. It sets the rest. None sent: the count in the contract stands.

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The lot lead gets the check-in code when the attendants arrive, 30 minutes before the first car. A planner or a day-of contact can get the code instead, when a mobile is given for them.
pf.visit.check-in at the kitchen: The code at the lot office for a plan walk-through, or the lead types it.
pf.visit.delivery and setup: The attendants set the stand and tickets at the drop-off curb, and park the cars for the hours booked. Nothing is left at the venue.
pf.visit.alcohol: The attendants never drink while working. A driver who looks unfit to drive is not given keys.
pf.visit.work changes at the event: More cars or more attendant hours only with the customer's written yes by text, at the rate shown before booking. No yes in 10 minutes: the stand keeps to the booked count.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The lot lead texts DONE when the last car is returned, with the car count and the hours worked.

starting answers: Events quoted from the valet plan: a signed contract, a deposit when booking, and the rest on the saved card when the night is done (the final car count sets it)

limits: Deposit cap: from the state form

Cancel schedule (the contract's): the deposit is kept once the date has been held 7 days; before that it's refunded
The business cancels, or the customer says no to a stand-in: a full refund
pf.money.service charge: A service charge, if the contract names one, is shown before the yes. It's never called a tip.
pf.money.tips: Guests may tip the attendants. Tips go to the attendants who worked the night, and are never added to a bill.
pf.money.tax: Sales tax where the state's rules tax the service, from the state form.
pf.money.Rosfield's $2: Applies, as for every kind of work.

pf.messages.never in a text: Key-box codes, gate codes, card details, and any name of a guest or a car owner beyond the ticket. Those stay on the secure page.

roles: Attendant (a driver's license for the lot's cars, where the rules ask)
pf.staff.supervision: A lot lead is on site at each event, and the lead reports to Sam.
pf.staff.who OKs what: Sam OKs every event date, any new lot, any car count change over 10%, and any price made for one event.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another attendant with a driver's license for the lot's cars. A lead the customer asked for by name is asked first; nobody moves on silence.
pf.staff.who does what (the example): Jo leads the valet nights; Nico works the curb. Dana and Lou run the lot office and the walk-throughs.

pf.rules.written contract: The valet contract, filled in from the booking, signed by the customer and Sam before any money is taken, for every event.
pf.rules.date hold: An event date stays saved while the contract is signed: up to 24 hours here, the owner's setting.
pf.rules.events a day: One lot: one event night at a time. The owner sets any other limit.
pf.rules.final count: Due 7 days before, on the secure page. It sets the rest, charged when the night is done. Over 10% more cars needs Sam's OK.
pf.rules.cancel schedule: Free to cancel for 7 days after signing. After that the deposit is kept, under the contract's dated schedule. One free date change, if the lot is free that night.
pf.rules.permits: The company's own registration; a valet or street permit where the city or venue requires one, filed as the contract says.
pf.rules.alcohol: The attendants never serve or carry alcohol; the venue's own bar is the venue's.
pf.rules.records: Contracts, permits and payments kept 7 years, as for every kind of work. Ticket logs deleted 30 days after the event.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for valet:
valet: A car is damaged: the attendant notes it on the ticket with a photo, and Sam handles the claim under the company's insurance
A car won't start or has a flat: the lead moves it, and the owner is called
The lot fills before the last car: the stand stops new cars, and the venue's rules decide the rest
An attendant can't come: another with a driver's license for the lot's cars, or a trusted stand-in if the customer agrees
Weather on the night: rain or high wind stops the stand while it lasts; the contract's weather rule decides the money
A driver who looks unfit to drive: no keys are given back; the lead calls the owner and the venue
The customer moves the date: one free move, if the lot is free that night
A car's owner says a bag or item is missing: the ticket log is checked, and Sam decides the next step
